subject: pathology
title: Philadelphia Chromosome in ALL, t(12;21), FAB and WHO Classification, Flow Cytometry

steps.tx: The Philadelphia chromosome, t(9;22) creating BCR-ABL, transforms B-ALL into a high risk disease of older children and adults with high presenting counts, historically demanding transplant, now softened by tyrosine kinase inhibitors added to chemotherapy. Its presence defines **Philadelphia-positive ALL**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Philadelphia positive ALL was the worst childhood subtype; kinase inhibitors plus chemotherapy rewrote its prognosis.

vis.caption: BCR-ABL pathogenesis, the Philadelphia fusion shared by CML and Philadelphia positive ALL.

steps.tx: In contrast, t(12;21) creating ETV6-RUNX1 hides cytogenetically yet marks the commonest and most favourable childhood B-ALL, detectable only by FISH or molecular tests because the translocation is cryptic on karyotype. The favourable cryptic fusion is **ETV6-RUNX1 from t(12;21)**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: ETV6-RUNX1 is invisible on karyotype yet commonest and kindest in childhood ALL; ask for FISH or PCR.

steps.tx: The old FAB classification sorted ALL by blast size and cytoplasm into L1, L2, and L3 and AML by maturation lines, useful morphology that genetics has since demoted to description rather than destiny. That morphology first system is the **FAB classification (French-American-British)**.
steps.say: FAB described what blasts look like; modern classification asks what genes they carry instead.

steps.tx: Modern WHO and International Consensus classifications build acute leukaemia entities around defining genetic abnormalities, differentiation states, and predispositions, because those features predict behaviour and select drugs better than appearance alone. The genetics first framework is the **WHO classification of haematolymphoid tumours**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: WHO entities are built on genetics because genetics predicts behaviour and chooses drugs better than morphology.

right.title: Genetics answers
points: Transplant need in AML and ALL

steps.tx: Flow cytometry fires laser interrogated antibodies at thousands of cells per second, mapping CD markers into lineage, maturation stage, and aberrant phenotypes that later serve as fingerprints for residual disease tracking. The multiparameter method is **flow cytometry immunophenotyping**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Flow cytometry gives every leukaemia a CD fingerprint at diagnosis and then hunts that fingerprint as MRD.

vis.caption: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, whose diagnosis now rests on flow cytometry lineage panels.

steps.tx: A diagnostic panel separates B precursor ALL, T-ALL, AML, and mixed phenotype acute leukaemia by cytoplasmic and surface markers, with mixed phenotype requiring stringent criteria because therapy borrows from both lineages. The biphenotypic category is **mixed phenotype acute leukaemia (MPAL)**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Mixed phenotype acute leukaemia is a stringent flow diagnosis, not a wastebasket for confusing panels.

rows: Treat with ALL based regimens often

steps.tx: Cytogenetic risk in childhood ALL assigns intensity: hyperdiploidy and ETV6-RUNX1 receive less, hypodiploidy and BCR-ABL-like signatures receive more, sparing cured children late toxicity. That balancing is **genetic risk stratification in ALL**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Good genetics earn gentler therapy in childhood ALL; sparing late toxicity is a deliberate treatment goal.

nodes.label: Intensity adjusted to risk and response

steps.tx: Adults with ALL fare worse from adverse genetics, comorbidity, and protocol tolerance, so paediatric inspired regimens, kinase inhibitors for Philadelphia disease, and immunotherapies such as blinatumomab increasingly bridge them to transplant or cure. The adult strategy shift is **paediatric-inspired ALL therapy in adults**.
steps.say: Adults borrow paediatric intensity, kinase inhibitors, and bispecific antibodies to close the ALL survival gap.
